why: The route page describes a rock arete on the Grand Teton's upper mountain with no glacier named, and the usual way down and out is the Garnet Canyon rock-and-trail line, not a glacier.
The descent crosses the Isella Glacier along a rock and moraine walkway, but no page I could read says whether crevasses or roping apply there.

The peak is reached only by the Bailey Range high route, where mid-July to mid-August parties carried strap-on crampons for snowfields, and Wikipedia notes an unnamed small glacier on its north slope.
A June trip report on Rock Mountain found continuous snow from about 4,800 ft, and June is inside this route's stated season, though July-Sep may be bare.
The only Tailgunner reports are on sites that refuse access, so no readable page settles whether the line is snow-free in its normal season.
A mid-July forum report found the couloir mostly melted out with bypassable ice patches and no crampons needed, and the route page itself says it melts out fairly quickly.
